evals.name: laravel-checkout
evals.prompt: We run a Laravel 11 event ticketing app and just got InnBucks merchant test credentials (API key, username, password and a test base URL). Add InnBucks as a payment option: a service class, config, a checkout page that shows what the customer needs, and whatever is needed to find out when the ticket is paid. Save the files.
evals.expected_output: A Laravel service, config, checkout view and queued job that log in with X-Api-Key + bearer token, generate a PAYMENT code in integer cents, show code, QR, *569#, countdown and a deep link, and check the code every 30 s in a job, fulfilling only on Claimed or Paid.

assertions.text: Every request sends X-Api-Key, and every request except POST /auth/third-party sends Authorization: Bearer <token>
The access token is cached and refreshed before 15 minutes (or re-obtained on a 401 with a single retry), not fetched per request
The amount is sent to POST /api/code/generate as integer cents (e.g. 450 for US$4.50), with type PAYMENT
The checkout shows the code, the QR image from qrCode, the *569# / app instruction and a 10-minute countdown
A mobile deep link is built from config: zw.co.innbucksnova.test://purchase?paymentToken={code} in test, com.innbucks.customer://purchase?paymentToken={code} in production
Status is checked with POST /api/code/inquiry at most every 30 seconds, from a queued job or scheduler rather than a tight loop in the web request
The order is marked paid on status Claimed (and Paid), and Expired / Timed Out are treated as final unpaid

evals.name: amount-bug
evals.expected_output: Explains that InnBucks amounts are integer cents, so 45 is 45 cents; convert with Math.round(total*100), prefer storing cents, and put the order reference in narration.

assertions.text: States that InnBucks amounts are integer cents / minor units
Converts to cents with rounding (e.g. Math.round(order.total * 100)) or recommends storing totals in cents, and does not send decimals
Points out that narration should carry the unique order reference because it appears on the merchant statement

evals.name: token-expiry
evals.prompt: Our Python service integrates the InnBucks Merchant API. It logs in once at startup and stores the token in a global. Everything works for a while, then every InnBucks call returns 401 until we restart the service. Why, and what's the right fix?
evals.expected_output: The bearer token expires after 15 minutes; cache it with its issue time, re-login after ~14 minutes and on a 401 re-login and retry once, sharing the token across workers.

assertions.text: Identifies that InnBucks access tokens expire after 15 minutes by default
Proposes proactive re-login before expiry (around 14 minutes) and re-login plus a single retry on 401
Keeps sending X-Api-Key on the login request and on every call

evals.name: agent-deposit
evals.prompt: We're an InnBucks agent. Build the cash deposit flow for our Django back office: the teller enters the customer's phone number and the cash amount, and the customer's wallet gets credited. Our network is flaky, so handle the case where we don't get a response.
evals.expected_output: Linked account inquiry (000 = success) then manual national ID check then deposit with a saved unique reference; on timeout never resend, use deposit inquiry on /bank/api/transaction/inquiry with originalParticipantReference and a new participantReference.

assertions.text: Uses GET /api/v1/account/msisdn/{msisdn}/details?currency=... first and treats responseCode 000 as success
Requires the teller to verify the returned name against the customer's national ID before depositing
Generates and saves a unique reference before POST /api/transaction/deposit, with amount in integer cents
On timeout/no response it does not resend the deposit but calls POST /bank/api/transaction/inquiry with originalParticipantReference = the deposit reference and a new participantReference
Reads the deposit outcome from details.responseCode of the inquiry response

evals.name: review-before-uat
evals.prompt: Please review our InnBucks integration before we submit UAT. We poll /api/code/inquiry every 3 seconds from the browser via our API, mark orders paid when status == 'Paid', and if the customer asks for another code we just generate a new one and stop tracking the old one. Refunds: we call /api/transaction/reversal/v2 with the payment's reference.
evals.expected_output: Flags: poll at most every 30 s server-side; treat Claimed as paid too; keep checking the old code; reversal only works for deposits, code payments use InnBucks' manual reversal process; mentions UAT video and sign-off.

assertions.text: Says code inquiries must be at most once every 30 seconds per code (InnBucks' explicit requirement)
Says status Claimed must also be treated as paid (not only Paid)
Says the old code must still be checked because the customer may pay it
Says the reversal endpoint is only for deposits and code payments go through InnBucks' manual reversal process
Mentions the UAT sign-off form with InnBucks references and the 1-2 minute customer journey video
